summary: The authors’ R script exports the default normothermia-minus-torpor coefficient under a torpor-minus-normothermia filename. The eight labeled GEO libraries independently support that direction. After aligning the full torpor worksheet, 12,932 of 15,099 published Explorer effects agree in direction (85.65%) and neither author-concordance-v2 route passes.

manualReview.summary: Author code explains the reversed sign in the published torpor results
manualReview.note: File2statistics.R sorts the default results(dds) and exports that object. The explicit SPHT-minus-SPNT result goes into a different object. Under the recorded R and DESeq2 defaults the exported coefficient is SPNT minus SPHT. The paper uses SPNT as the torpor baseline in Tables 3 and 4 and Supplementary Table S3. The comparison preserves each workbook coefficient at stored precision and inverts it once for the registered contrast. The mouse GeneID join, both orientations and missing statistics are recorded in data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE179663/codex-2026-11-21/results.json.
reviewFlags: After orientation, Pearson 0.805081, Spearman 0.829910 and directional agreement 85.65% fall below the policy cutoffs.

The archived inventory omits Samples_SPHTvsSPNT.csv. Supplementary Tables S1 and S2, GEO and ENA support the sample assignments. Count-derived base means verify the eight libraries as a set. The labeled HT/NT count ratios and the export code support the biological direction.
The authors fit a group-only DESeq2 model with transcript-length offsets. The registered edgeR-QL model adjusts for sex and uses TMM and different filtering.

verificationReview.reason: The prefilter and normalization reproduced 16,195 author GeneIDs and their workbook base means. The script exports the default SPNT-minus-SPHT coefficient. After aligning to registered SPHT minus SPNT, Pearson is 0.805081, Spearman is 0.829910 and 12,932 of 15,099 directions agree. Neither v2 route passes. At adjusted P < 0.05, 227 genes occur in both discovery lists (759 author, 278 published Explorer). Zfp729b has a registered discovery and missing author adjusted P.
verificationReview.nextStep: Use the full-table comparison for the registered contrast and retain Table S3 as a selected historical comparison. Materialize the reviewed normalized input with refute/orient.py --write before replacing the selected-panel specification and regenerating comparison records.

comparabilityReview.basis: Compare all published edgeR-QL effects to the corresponding DESeq2 coefficients at the precision stored in the full SP_HTvsNT worksheet, using the authors’ projected mouse GeneIDs. Orient the coefficient once from SPNT minus SPHT to SPHT minus SPNT. results.json records the full literal comparison and the separate Table S3 comparison.
comparabilityReview.reference: Ulm DOI 10.18725/OPARU-45070, File2statistics.R lines 25–49, File3results.xlsx worksheet SP_HTvsNT columns A–J, and ReadMe.pdf. Author S1/S2 animal and accession tables, GEO RSEM/metadata and ENA runs identify the biological groups.

cohort.note: Eight individual short-photoperiod hamsters provided whole hypothalamus near ZT04. SPHT02, SPHT10, SPHT26 and SPHT33 were in torpor (one female, three males). SPNT19, SPNT36, SPNT37 and SPNT38 were normothermic (two females, two males). Four long-photoperiod animals fall outside the registered comparison. Table S1 documents sex, state and terminal temperature. Table S2, GEO, ENA and the registered sample sheet link the animals to their libraries. The original statistical input CSV is absent from the archived inventory.

contrast.note: The script names the SPHT and SPNT groups and uses the default factor order. It exports the sorted default DESeq2 result, which gives SPNT relative to SPHT. Count-derived HT/NT ratios from the independently labeled libraries run opposite to the workbook for 16,112 of 16,191 evaluable genes. The aligned author column negates the literal effect exactly once.

features.note: The join uses the authors’ mouse GeneIDs and the registered feature map. Each of the 15,099 published symbols maps to a unique GeneID. This recovers 409 pairs with different symbol strings. Of 1,096 author GeneIDs absent from the published output, 1,088 have mapped symbols and eight lack a mapped symbol. All eight unmapped features were tested in the registered fit.

effects.note: Both coefficients measure log2 fold change between the same biological states. In the registered direction, Pearson is 0.805081 and Spearman is 0.829910. All 15,099 pairs are nonzero and 12,932 agree in direction (85.65%). Median absolute log2FC difference is 0.041932 and the local-to-author RMS effect ratio is 0.805014. Before alignment the two correlations were negative and 2,167 directions agreed.

inference.note: The authors used a group-only DESeq2 Wald test, rounded RSEM counts, tximport effective-length offsets and a rounded row-sum filter of at least 10. The registered edgeR-QL fit used fractional counts, filterByExpr, TMM and a sex covariate. Its FDR family included 15,107 tested rows, of which 15,099 have published symbols. Among shared genes, 15,088 raw-P pairs and 14,599 adjusted-P pairs are finite. At adjusted P < 0.05, 759 author and 277 registered calls are evaluable in both tables, including 227 shared. One additional registered call, Zfp729b (GeneID 100416706), has missing author adjusted P. Its author call is unassessed.

coverage.note: The complete torpor worksheet contains 16,195 finite effects. The join covers 15,099/15,099 registered genes and 15,099/16,195 author genes (93.23%). SP_HTvsNT_reg is a significance-filtered tab. The 68 predefined indicator genes in article Table S3 are a separate, selected reference.

comparabilityReview.criteria: Use all finite effects from the full torpor worksheet, unique GeneIDs, the code-defined sign and the fixed author-concordance-v2 rules. At least 30 pairs and 90% output coverage are required. Both correlations must reach 0.90, or at least 90% of at least 30 nonzero pairs must agree in direction with nonzero pairs covering at least 90% of the join. Require biological and feature compatibility. Treat P, FDR and magnitude differences as context.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: The export code and independently labeled count ratios support the sign correction. Both concordance routes fall below their thresholds on the complete published output. The pipelines differ in normalization, filtering and model design. Their individual contributions to the residual discrepancies were not measured. Full verification remains unsigned.

additionalComparisonSpec.authorMethod: DESeq2 1.22.2 Wald test, group-only design, tximport 1.10.1 RSEM with length offsets
additionalComparisonSpec.orientation: HT_minus_NT_log2FC contains the negation of the literal SPNT-minus-SPHT workbook coefficient. The comparison uses that already aligned column with multiplier +1. workbook_log2FC preserves the literal effect and author_padj preserves the author’s adjusted P.
additionalComparisonSpec.note: The full SP_HTvsNT worksheet contains all effects after the authors’ count prefilter. review.py extracts the worksheet and maps its mouse GeneIDs to unique registered symbols. refute/orient.py appends the sign-aligned column from that pinned extraction. Both signs and all missing test cells are retained. The adjusted-P lists overlap at 227/810 across complete lists and 227/809 within pairs with finite adjusted P. Eight unmapped fit rows contribute to the registered FDR family and have no published coefficients.

openIssues: The archived deposit inventory omits Samples_SPHTvsSPNT.csv. The eight libraries are supported by the count replay. Their group assignments are supported by the animal and accession records and the labeled count ratios.
The remaining effect and inference differences have not been attributed to individual pipeline choices. Neither numerical acceptance route passes.
